artifact.name: 15-reconstruction-relevance
artifact.purpose: Research-only assessment of which recovered types and interfaces should anchor future clean-room OpenSpore reconstruction.

assessments.rationale: The reference record joins instance identity, serializer state, intrusive resource ownership, and a counter. Those relationships are needed to reproduce Cell content identity and lifetime even when storage is modernized.

reuse.fallback_basis: Referenced by every major Cell content record and by cCellGame world/serializable state.

assessments.rationale: These records carry Cell tuning, AI, food, populate, effect-map, and global initialization data. Field order and fixed/variable array boundaries are compatibility data, not implementation code.

reuse.fallback_basis: The records are explicit inputs to cCellGame, cCellGFX, population, combat, advect, and world construction.

assessments.rationale: DBPF package/index locking and record access are mechanically important but replaceable. Preserve record identity, bounds, priority, and errors; do not reproduce the original object graph or index implementation.
PFRecordRead is a bounded record adapter under the resource manager. Its byte-facing read result matters, while its internal cursor/index representation does not.

The type/group/instance triple is the stable content identity used by Cell, world, empire, missions, editor, rendering, and persistence. It should remain an explicit value type at every future boundary.

reuse.fallback_basis: The SDK embeds ResourceKey in numerous high-value owners and collections across every major subsystem.

assessments.rationale: Lookup priority, enumeration, cache invalidation, and key identity are semantic boundaries; the manager's hash/index/cache implementation is replaceable infrastructure.
Scale bucket, strength, variance, period, and advect identity drive Cell world selection and motion. Preserve the decoded record and lookup semantics; do not import original code.

reuse.fallback_basis: Nested in cCellWorldResource and consumed by GetNextAdvectID/current-advect paths.

assessments.rationale: The 20,964-byte object owns world references, the 4096-cell pool, player index, serializable data, timing, lock, and update state. Exact offsets are an oracle/replacement anchor; behavior remains to be reconstructed from bounded evidence.

reuse.fallback_basis: One named initializer reaches 22 callees; many other unknown Cell functions access the same global state without exact type association.

assessments.rationale: World/layer creation order, preload associations, effects, and display activation are observable. The very large internal GFX object graph and RenderWare implementation are not gameplay contracts.
assessments.semantic_owner: Cell world, layer, model, and effect composition

assessments.rationale: Initialize, enter, update, input callbacks, exit, and disposal define stage activation and ordering. Preserve those operations and transition order, not the original singleton/global ABI.

reuse.fallback_basis: Lifecycle methods are virtual; 13 functions are attributed to the family and the candidate derived table has 27 slots.

assessments.rationale: The 920-byte object is the identity, transform, target, resource, animation, health, AI, chase/flee, scale, query, and GFX record for each Cell. Its offsets are high-value compatibility facts even though this campaign does not implement the class.

reuse.fallback_basis: Central pooled entity consumed by movement, creation, lifecycle, combat, query, animation, and GFX functions.

assessments.rationale: The linked-pool data and 28-byte query entry define nearby-cell candidate semantics. OpenSpore may use another arena, but must preserve position, radius, identity, and iteration behavior.

reuse.fallback_basis: Owned by foreground/background cCellGame query pools and consumed by interaction/combat paths.

assessments.rationale: The record owns Cell progression, unlocked parts, counters, play time, game/difficulty identity, mission state, and tutorial flags. Exact serialization boundaries matter for future compatibility.

reuse.fallback_basis: Referenced by cCellGame initialization and the ISimulatorSerializable interface.

assessments.rationale: Cell HUD state, world/background vectors, zoom, selection, and rollover lifecycle are observable. The original object layout and UTFWin implementation are not necessary if equivalent UI behavior is provided.
The header points to scale-level and advect arrays that determine Cell world population and flow selection. Decode and preserve those relationships even before runtime execution is reconstructed.

reuse.fallback_basis: Primary Cell world reference in cCellGame and input to advect/level selection functions.

assessments.rationale: The citizen is a core creature/social participant inside tribes and colonies. Preserve identity, membership, needs, abilities, and lifecycle interfaces; the complete 4 KB layout is not automatically a gameplay requirement.

reuse.fallback_basis: Referenced by cTribe member collections and creature/social progression.

assessments.rationale: Buildings, population, vehicles, updates, and city lifecycle are semantic. The original 36-slot ABI and building-object graph may be replaced once the state transitions are identified.

The 58-slot surface spans targets, abilities, animation, effects, movement, social behavior, and gameplay callbacks. Preserve the semantic operations and dispatch order, not the complete original object memory image.
Brain level, evolution points, ability mode, learned abilities, glide state, and normalizing scale are explicit progression state. Exact offsets are useful for reconstruction and differential work.

Political identity, population, position, members, tools, planners, food, timers, and progression make cTribe a core persistent social-state record. Layout recovery is valuable, but no reconstruction is authorized here.

reuse.fallback_basis: SDK structure plus high-value dossiers and shared-state consumers place it in tribe/civ and event paths.

assessments.rationale: Send versus post and the packed editor-model/event payload are useful semantic boundaries. The concrete allocator and temporary object implementation are replaceable.
Creature lookup, target position/angle, and controller/animation association are semantic. Container internals may be modernized.
Current/real target position, current/target angle, movement, rotation, and update interpolation are the controller contract. Exact singleton/object storage is not necessary.
Creation identity, parts, colors, names, history, and model transitions are editor semantics. The original virtual object graph can be replaced after contracts are frozen.
Play-mode input, actor callbacks, environment reactions, and update sequencing are semantic. The 22 KB concrete object layout is not required unless byte-level compatibility is chosen.

cEditor is the input/message/update/edit-history boundary and reaches 494 distinct callees across editor, UI, resources, graphics, and gameplay. Preserve its semantic command surface, not the original object memory or UTFWin hierarchy.

Position, orientation, model, animation IDs, blend/loop state, and anim-world ownership are the useful contract. The original 32-slot ABI and model objects are replaceable behind an animation interface.

reuse.fallback_basis: The 32-slot vtable is called through cEditorAnimWorld/IAnimWorld and carries 18 named fields.

assessments.rationale: Load/update/destroy creature operations and model/effect world binding are useful semantic interfaces. Implementations and object ownership are replaceable.

reuse.fallback_basis: The 23-slot interface anchors the editor and general animation dispatch surface.

assessments.rationale: Window/proc/drawable behavior can be supplied by a modern UI toolkit. Preserve event identity, command IDs, hierarchy effects, and mode routing, not the original 71-slot ABI.

reuse.fallback_basis: UTFWin Window has 99 attributed family functions; IWindow supplies the 71-slot surface.

assessments.rationale: Parent/child windows, proc lists, areas, controls, cursor, caption, and drawables define UI behavior, but the original framework can be replaced. Only externally meaningful commands and dispatch survive.

Political ID, identity color, names, archetype/trait, allies/enemies, home system, money, culture, and progression form the empire identity record. Its layout is persistent and shared across space, relationships, missions, and events.

reuse.fallback_basis: Only three named methods are exact associations, but shared-state roots and dossier evidence show broad owner-wide use.

assessments.rationale: Mission identity, state, timing, owners/targets, rewards, unlocks, costs, progress events, properties, and communication links are both serialized state and transition semantics.

reuse.fallback_basis: Owned/tracked by cMissionManager and referenced by empire/planet/communication state.

assessments.rationale: Availability, selection, tracking, recent mission lists, configuration, limits, and gaps are semantic transitions. Internal storage can be replaced after transition contracts are established.
Relationship value, flags, and event modifiers form the durable directed-pair state. Exact field semantics are needed to preserve war/alliance transitions.

reuse.fallback_basis: Stored in cRelationshipManager and directly mutated by war/peace/alliance functions.

assessments.rationale: Directed political-ID lookup, war/alliance/peace transitions, decay queues, and event modifiers are semantic. The map/container implementation is replaceable.
Count, type, cost, uniqueness, political/position IDs, properties, resource key, and message links define cargo/trade identity. The object crosses economy, events, and persistence.
Active planet/star, relationship manager, current context, player empire ID/cache, rotation, and colonies form a compact cross-stage identity spine. Exact offsets anchor several unknown roots.

reuse.fallback_basis: Directly backs roots 01021260, 01021080, and 01021300 with 262/175/182 total callers respectively.

assessments.rationale: Spices, rare maps/groups, NPC stores, newly available commodities, and mode identity define trade behavior. Internal maps and strategy vtables may be replaced behind that contract.
Route presence and map data are semantic, but the route algorithm is unresolved. Characterize the interface before deciding whether layout or implementation matters.

Resource points, ownership, capture/convert/buy state, and percentages are gameplay-facing. The full object can remain behind a typed planet-resource interface unless binary replacement requires offsets.

reuse.fallback_basis: Owned by cPlanetRecord and consumed by trading/capture/conversion systems.

assessments.rationale: Message ID, name, creature, block, and scalar parameters form a concrete cross-boundary payload. Preserve field order and payload meaning once IDs are named.

reuse.fallback_basis: SDK record bridges editor events to AnimatedCreature/IAnimWorld dispatch.

assessments.rationale: Communication event identity, sender/receiver, arguments, and queue/display transitions are semantic. Numeric message/action IDs and mode-specific records remain unresolved.

reuse.fallback_basis: Allocated and enqueued by cCommManager; also related to unknown space event-record pairs.

assessments.rationale: Current event, event lists, message listener, cancellation conditions, creation, handling, and display are semantic. Container internals are replaceable.
Send, post, listener/handler registration, priority, locking, and ordered queue processing are semantic routing contracts. The original ABI and storage are replaceable.

reuse.fallback_basis: Only the Get accessor is exact; six vtable-family rows and the 19-slot interface establish broader reach.

assessments.rationale: Queue entries, priorities, listeners, handlers, lock/remove/process operations, and post/send distinctions are semantic. Internal queue objects are replaceable.

reuse.fallback_basis: Most use is virtual/data dispatch and therefore underrepresented by direct-call metrics.

assessments.rationale: Event-log entries, timestamps, icons/text, lifetime, and display are semantic; storage and UI widgets are replaceable.
AI/behavior registration, update, and event delivery determine gameplay decisions. The concrete manager object and vtable can be replaced by an injected service.
Game-data ID, definition ID, owner, and political ID form a recurring identity/persistence base across tribes, inventory, cities, commodities, tools, and missions.

Input state, current/previous mode, maps, mouse values, regions, strings, and callbacks are explicit field/vtable facts. A future interface should preserve normalized events and routing, while raw layout is valuable for compatibility and static typing.
Registration, active index, mode identity/name, camera/viewer, set/get operations, and exit-before-enter ordering are central semantic contracts. The global registry layout is replaceable.
Noun identity, data materialization, model updates, and player/noun lookup are semantic. Exact map/node internals are replaceable once root 00b21340 is characterized.
Save/load coordination is semantically important, but the service implementation is replaceable. First characterize ownership, transaction boundaries, and serializable graph traversal.
Frame time, delta conversion, pause count, speed, and update order determine deterministic behavior. Expose typed clock operations rather than reproduce the manager object.
Viewer, camera, projection, and view-ray services affect movement and presentation. Preserve normalized camera/ray operations; replace concrete graphics objects.

Data pointer, next-free index, identifier, capacities, object size, and lifetime metadata define pool-index identity used by Cell replacement and creation. Exact offsets are valuable; allocator policy is not sacred.
The root owns or coordinates global Simulator services. Preserve service lookup/lifecycle semantics through dependency injection; do not reproduce the singleton registry implementation.
Global/local property-list ownership, preloading, creation, and reference tracking are infrastructure. Typed property keys, lookup, enumeration, and stream behavior are the semantic boundary.

reuse.fallback_basis: The 25 vtable-family rows and pointer-mediated use are underrepresented by direct calls.

assessments.rationale: Direct-property storage is an optimization beneath the property contract. Preserve lookup, typed values, parent behavior, and stream compatibility; the concrete layout may be replaced.

Reference counting, cast identity, read/write, noun identity, and related hooks define the serializable-object contract. Preserve operations and ordering, not the original three-pointer inheritance layout.

reuse.fallback_basis: The 9-slot vtable is embedded by cEmpire, cStarRecord, cMissionManager, cMission, and cCellSerializableData.

assessments.rationale: The exported size is the small wrapper/union representation, while its typed value forms include booleans, numbers, strings, vectors, keys, transforms, and arrays. Exact stream encoding and typed access semantics are the contract, not the original getter family.

Sorted entries, parent fallback, operation count, ownership, read/write, and property IDs determine configuration and save behavior. Preserve the stream and inheritance semantics; container internals may later be modernized behind a tested codec.
The serializable header carries current planet and other save identity. Its stream position and field order are compatibility facts even when the rest of persistence is redesigned.

reuse.fallback_basis: Named serializable save header in the SDK and simulator persistence path.

assessments.rationale: The unresolved global-slot/accessor family underpins much of Simulator. Characterize return values, ownership, and use domains before assigning any concrete class; never infer implementation from fan-in.

reuse.fallback_basis: The three roots are treated as one semantic family; individual caller sets overlap conceptually but are not claimed as a union count.

assessments.rationale: The 4,384 unknown-vtable implementation rows can unlock broad dispatch semantics, but identity is unresolved and 14 rows carry gameplay logic. Vtable-owner mapping should precede body reconstruction.

reuse.fallback_basis: Corpus count is exact; caller/callee unions are intentionally not invented for unattributed functions.

assessments.rationale: The 6,527-caller release/forwarding wrapper and 2,901-caller construction wrapper are graph chokepoints, not gameplay types. Preserve allocator/reference behavior through modern infrastructure and do not anchor gameplay reconstruction on them.

reuse.fallback_basis: Caller totals are summed for leverage only; the two roots are not one gameplay interface.

assessments.rationale: Planet type/orbit, scores, species, commodities, tech, spice generation, terrain key, tribes, and colonies drive world identity and progression. Exact record layout is valuable for reconstruction and persistence.

reuse.fallback_basis: Only Create is exact-associated, but the record owns planet, species, commodity, colony, and empire-adjacent state.

assessments.rationale: Height, gravity, water, orientation, surface conversion, and nearest-city queries are the gameplay-facing planet model. The 92-byte wrapper is best treated as an interface over replaceable terrain/physics infrastructure.
Loading, binary stars, asteroids, celestial effects, and graphics are semantic system boundaries. Concrete effects and render objects are replaceable.
Last-observed time, empire/starter IDs, key, citizen species, profile, planets, and count define serializable star identity. Preserve layout for world generation and save compatibility.

reuse.fallback_basis: The record is embedded throughout cStarManager and planet generation even where exact function association is sparse.

assessments.rationale: Star grids, starter/saved records, empires, adventure IDs, generation rules, political IDs, trade routes, relationships, and transactions form a major semantic manager. Internal storage is replaceable after state transitions are frozen.

Terrain generation, chunks, modifications, height queries, water, land, atmosphere, and render passes carry world behavior. RenderWare-specific structures and passes are replaceable infrastructure; semantic terrain queries are not.

reuse.fallback_basis: Nine vtable-family rows supplement the 14 exact associations but are not added as methods.

classification_vocabulary.replaceable-infrastructure: A modern equivalent may replace the original implementation. Only externally observable identity, ordering, data, error, and event contracts cross the boundary.
classification_vocabulary.reproduce-layout: The byte layout, field offsets, record order, or serialized identity is itself reconstruction evidence and should be preserved in future clean-room compatibility work. This campaign records the decision only and implements nothing.
classification_vocabulary.semantic-interface-only: Operations, identity, state transitions, event ordering, and cross-subsystem meaning matter; the original in-memory class layout and vtable ABI need not be reproduced.

domain_summary.finding: ResourceKey and Cell record layouts are semantic compatibility data; DBPF/resource-manager internals are replaceable.
cCellGame, cCellObjectData, serializable data, world/advect records, and references are the Cell reconstruction spine; UI/GFX are interface contracts.
Creature, progression, tribe, citizen, and city types anchor social simulation; only compact identity/progression layouts are byte-critical.
Planet/star records are persistent layout anchors; cPlanetModel, cStarManager, cSolarSystem, and cTerrainSphere are semantic service boundaries.
SpacePlayerData, cEmpire, relationship data, mission, inventory, and route/trade types anchor identity, economy, and persistence.
Editor/animation interfaces are semantic; UTFWin internals are replaceable, with event/command behavior retained.
Message, communication, animation, and UI-log records need explicit payloads and ordering before their storage can be modernized.
Input, mode, time, behavior, noun, pool, and game-data roots are foundational; singleton lookup functions are wrappers, not interfaces to copy.
Property/PropertyList and serializable contracts are cross-system spines; cPropManager and direct storage are replaceable.
Unresolved service slots and vtables unlock many functions; generic allocation wrappers do not unlock gameplay semantics.

evidence_policy.decisions: The report classifies reconstruction value, not implementation readiness or original semantic truth.
evidence_policy.ghidra: No program was open during final verification, so no live Ghidra claim was added. Existing pinned Ghidra/SDK exports and research dossiers are evidence only.
evidence_policy.runtime: No original-game runtime trace supports these assessments. All function fan-in/out and interface conclusions are static and may miss dynamic dispatch or runtime-populated tables.
evidence_policy.sdk: SDK names, layouts, fields, and vtable slots establish reference provenance. They do not establish behavior, ownership, or ABI truth by themselves.

interface_anchors.reason: Owns player identity, pool handles, world/plane state, movement targets, and ordered interaction events.
Mode registration, activation ordering, frame ticking, shutdown, and injected host services.
The 614-caller input manager and 27-slot vtable are the strongest input/mode state anchor.
Typed input, camera/view, behavior, mode, persistence, and frame-clock operations replace raw global getters.
ResourceKey identity and record bytes are semantic; DBPF indexes, caches, and package locks are replaceable.
Typed keys, parent fallback, enumeration, and versioned read/write behavior anchor configuration and persistence.
Read/write/noun/refcount operations span empire, star, mission, and Cell save state without requiring the original inheritance ABI.
Ordered key/mouse/window/message routing and mode transitions must survive UTFWin/message-manager replacement.
Creature load/update/destroy and animation state/pose operations bridge editor and rendering.
SpacePlayerData, current-empire cache, political ID, and star-manager registry unlock a large unknown space/empire region.
War/alliance transitions, trade inventory, and mission state are high-value space interfaces; internals remain replaceable.
Retains command/window semantics while allowing UTFWin, RenderWare, and D3D implementations to be replaced.

limitations: No function-level original runtime trace exists; semantic understanding is not promoted to OBSERVED or VERIFIED.
SporeApp.exe has no MSVC RTTI, so class hierarchy and vtable ownership are incomplete.
The canonical function manager iterator has 58,757 entries while the live manager count previously reported 59,245; all type metrics use the frozen 58,757-row corpus.
Only 172/2,149 gameplay functions have persisted decompilation, and all persisted exports carry unknown-calling-convention warnings.
Type-level xrefs are not directly exported. Reuse metrics associate canonical functions through exact SDK struct_names; data-only types use a lower-confidence structural fallback.
Distinct caller/callee unions do not prove runtime reachability and can double-count a caller across methods only in sum_function_fan_in/out; union fields are preferred.
Function association is name/struct provenance, not proof that every SDK function has the expected receiver type or that every vtable family label is correct.
SDK layouts include imported or incomplete fields; exact field semantics remain bounded by decompilation, dossiers, and absent runtime evidence.
The Ghidra MCP connection had no open program at final verification, so no new live query was available.
The assessment intentionally does not rank implementation effort or authorize implementation.

association.direct: A type's function set is the exact set of canonical rows whose sdk_vtable.struct_names contains the assessed SDK type path.
association.null_fallback: If no direct function association exists, metrics are null and the reuse score uses R-2; zero is not substituted for unknown.
association.vtable_family: Vtable-family counts are supplemental attribution and do not replace exact struct-name associations.

quantitative_reuse.R-1: Quantitative method: score 5 for >=100 distinct caller functions, >=100 distinct callee functions, or a pervasive value/interface with a broad documented owner graph; 4 for 40-99 callers/callees, 10-19 associated functions, 20+ vtable slots plus owner-wide use, or a high-fanout orchestrator; 3 for 10-39 relationships, 5-9 associated functions, or medium structural spread; 2 for 1-9 direct relationships or 2-4 functions; 1 for no observed direct reuse but a still-needed narrow boundary.
quantitative_reuse.R-2: Fallback method: when no exact type-associated function rows exist, estimate from explicit owner/field relations, vtable slots, documented consumers, and the count of dependent high-fan-in roots. The result is capped as uncertain and does not invent xrefs.
quantitative_reuse.UX-1: Unknown-unlock leverage: score 5 for >=200 gameplay callers, >=500 total callers, >=400 distinct callees from an anchor, or broad named interface ownership; 4 for 100-199 gameplay callers, 250-499 total callers, 200-399 distinct callees, or 20+ vtable slots; 3 for 25-99 gameplay callers, 50-249 total callers, 100-199 distinct callees, or a 10-19 method anchor; lower bands follow proportionally.
quantitative_reuse.UX-2: Corpus method: score by count of unresolved functions or root callers represented by the unknown corpus; it measures leverage, not semantic certainty.

scoring.GI-1: Gameplay importance scale: 5 = cross-stage identity, lifecycle, persistence, or core state; 4 = major stage/subsystem state or content; 3 = major bounded feature, editor, presentation, or content; 2 = supporting adapter/tool/event; 1 = peripheral or replaceable substrate.
scoring.score_scope: Scores assess future reconstruction value only. They are not confidence probabilities and do not imply this campaign should implement the type.
scoring.uncertainty: low = direct SDK layout plus multiple static artifacts; medium = static names/graphs with missing runtime or incomplete vtable/type evidence; high = data-only, unnamed, dynamically dispatched, or otherwise type-open.

source_precedence: Pinned binary identity and frozen triage/xref corpus
Ghidra decompilation as evidence, never as truth

method.stable_ordering: Top-level sections use fixed lexical order. Assessments use fixed domain order and stable authored IDs; provenance, complete sections, and domain summaries use fixed lexical or declared order. No timestamp or wall-clock field is present.

anchor_order.reason: Cross-stage identity and persistence contracts reduce the largest semantic unknowns.
Mode, input, behavior, clock, and persistence boundaries unlock dependent stage code.
These are the concrete Cell state, identity, pool, content, and save spine.
Stage and cross-stage gameplay owners should be characterized before their many dependent functions.
Editor, content, UI, animation, and property boundaries concentrate broad fan-out and can be modernized behind interfaces.

recommendation.campaign_constraint: Research only. This campaign implements none of the anchors and authorizes no source, binary, or Ghidra mutation.
highest_leverage_unknowns: FUN_00b3d300 global slot and exact pointee/consumer domains
FUN_00b3d2a0 global slot and adjacent manager identity
recommendation.summary: Anchor reconstruction on semantic state and interface contracts, not on global singleton wrappers or infrastructure chokepoints. Preserve byte layouts only where identity, replacement ABI, fixed-size records, or serialization require them.

scope.binary_access: No SPORE binary or asset was accessed by this assessment.

unknown_unlockers.unlock: Resolve global-slot ownership and consumer domains before dependent Simulator functions.
Resolve adjacent global-slot identity and its role in current-empire lookup.
Resolve scalar/handle semantics and forwarded object ownership.
Roots 01021260, 01021080, and 01021300 expose current planet, context, player ID, and lazy empire cache.
Characterize FUN_00b21340 before assigning a concrete cGameNounManager method identity.
21 named methods and 24 attributed vtable functions reach 494 distinct callees; input/message/tool ownership unlocks a large unknown region.
The 27-slot input/mode vtable and field map anchor the broadest direct gameplay dependency.
68 Property methods and 15 PropertyList methods connect configuration, content, and persistence to 74 distinct callees.
Vtable-owner mapping is a prerequisite for dispatch semantics across editor, app, resource, and UI code.
High graph leverage but only allocator/reference infrastructure; it must not anchor gameplay reconstruction.
